blocks.title: Backoff then DLQ
blocks.text: Nominal backoff ==1s-8s x5==, rounded up to the delay topics: attempts 1-2 at `retry-1m`, 3-4 at `retry-5m`, 5 at `retry-30m`, then ==DLQ==.

blocks.q: A producer POSTs a notification with idempotency_key K, times out, and retries with the same K. What stops the user getting two pushes, and what is the UNIQUE column on idempotency_key for?
a_bullets: The Redis `SET NX EX 24h` gate finds the existing key for the first request
The retry gets the original notification_id back with 202, and nothing new is enqueued
The UNIQUE column is only a per-partition backstop: the table is partitioned by created_at, so a retry in another partition would not collide
So the Redis gate is the dedup mechanism, not the UNIQUE index

blocks.q: A 2M-message marketing campaign is running and users report OTP texts arriving minutes late. All SMS traffic shares one queue. What is the bug and the fix?
a_bullets: OTPs sit behind the campaign messages in the same FIFO queue, so queue wait grows with the backlog
Use separate Kafka topics per channel x priority, so critical never queues behind bulk
Give critical its own consumer group, or weight consumption (for example 8:4:2:1)
Fan the campaign out at a throttled rate (for example 2k msgs/sec) into the bulk topic

blocks.q: A worker gets APNs 410 UNREGISTERED for one message and a Twilio 503 for another. Which one is retried, and what happens to the other?
a_bullets: Twilio 503 is transient: retry with exponential backoff and jitter, up to 5 attempts, then move to the DLQ
APNs 410 is permanent: the token is dead, so retrying can never succeed
For the 410, prune the device token and mark the message failed or suppressed
Retrying permanent errors only burns worker capacity and provider rate limits

blocks.q: The preference store goes down. An OTP and a marketing push both arrive. What should each do, and why not treat them the same?
a_bullets: OTP (critical) fails open: send it, because a blocked login costs more than a rare opt-out miss
Marketing fails closed: hold or drop it, because sending to someone who opted out is a legal risk (CAN-SPAM, TCPA)
Failure policy follows the cost of the wrong outcome, per priority
The same rule applies to the Redis rate limiter: open for critical, closed for bulk

blocks.q: Twilio webhooks for one SMS arrive as delivered, then sent. A naive handler overwrites status with each event. What does the user-facing status show, and how do you fix it?
a_bullets: The naive handler ends on sent, so a delivered message looks undelivered and the status goes backwards
Give each status a rank: queued < sent < delivered < opened < clicked
Upsert only when the new rank is higher, so out-of-order and duplicate webhooks are harmless
Keep every event in the append-only notification_events table, and poll the provider after 15 min if a webhook is missed
